estimator-bias-variability.alt: Three probability histograms on the same scale from 0.1 to 0.8, each with a dashed line at the true proportion p = 0.40. Top: the sample proportion from random samples of 25 is centered at 0.40 and spread widely, from about 0.2 to 0.6: unbiased, high variability. Middle: the sample proportion from random samples of 100 is centered at 0.40 and about half as spread out: unbiased, low variability. Bottom: a biased method whose sample proportions center at 0.55 with low variability: biased, low variability.
